note:
flashing the pinned reference image target/emu-ref/c976f17a9-esp32+test_cycle_probe/fw-esp32v3 rather than building one: this payload's claim is a comparison against an emulated run of the SAME bytes (DD30), and the tree this runner stands in is not that commit. `scripts/emu/build-reference-image.sh esp32,test_cycle_probe <commit> none` builds it in a detached worktree; the directory name is the provenance, and the runner checks its feature half.

THE SENTENCES ABOVE AND THE `source`/`capture` lines ARE THE RUNNER'S OWN; everything from here down was ADDED BY HAND at the desk (M5 P4, 2026-09-11). Nothing was changed, only added.

RECORDED, GATED BY NOTHING. This payload calibrates a time grade and never gates one. The classic's counter is CCOUNT — CPU cycles at 240 MHz — and there is no `lp-emu:esp32v3:t2` on this machine to calibrate against (ruling R1, and the director's E1 answer of 2026-09-11: `t1` only for G-classic, `t2` named as future work). Every figure here is that future calibration's INPUT, not a claim about the emulator, and no replay compares it.

DESK. Board `domraem/dom-z-102`, revision v3.1, MAC 30:76:f5:ec:f6:34, over the CH340K 1a86:7522 at locationID 0x1133000, port 3 of hub 0x1130000; the C6 on port 2 was not touched. espflash 3.3.0, `--timeout-secs 420`. espflash's own banner in the transcript confirms the part: `Chip type: esp32 (revision v3.1)`, `Crystal frequency: 40 MHz`, `Features: WiFi, BT, Dual Core, 240MHz, Coding Scheme None`.

THE CLOCK CHECKS OUT AGAINST ITSELF. `iram_loop` rep=1 reports `cycles=2500033 us=10417`, which is 240.0 cycles per microsecond — CCOUNT counting CPU cycles at the rated 240 MHz, with the payload's own microsecond bracket as the second reading. `bracket_overhead` is 33 cycles, and it is subtracted from nothing: it is recorded so a later model can.

TWO PAIRS COME BACK EQUAL, AND THAT IS THE FINDING TO CARRY FORWARD, not a bug in the capture. `iram_loop` and `flash_loop` are cycle-for-cycle identical (2,500,033 both, rep after rep), and so are `code_walk/cold` and `code_walk/warm` (2,230,489 both). On this part the flash-resident loop is served out of the instruction cache once it is warm and costs what the IRAM one costs, and the code walk is not large enough to evict itself between the two halves. A t2 model built from these two pairs would learn that flash and IRAM are free of each other, which is true of THIS walk and this cache state, and a calibration that wants the miss cost needs a walk larger than the cache — the `rodata_stride` ladder is where the cost does appear: 32,735,635 cycles at stride 16 against ~63.5-64.0 M at strides 32 through 4096, a factor of 1.95 between the first rung and the rest and then a flat plateau.

FIVE REPETITIONS PER KERNEL, NOTHING AVERAGED, exactly as the set intends: reps 0..=4 are all in the transcript and the `[fw-check-json]` records carry each one separately. The reps agree to the cycle on the compute kernels (`slice_shape` is 171,347 in every rep, its microsecond bracket moving by 1 us) — this part has no frequency scaling and nothing else was running, which is why a single figure is meaningful here in a way a heap figure on the shipped image is not.

SECOND BOOT. espflash hard-resets after writing, so this is the boot after the write. A harness image never mounts `lpfs`, so there is no first/second-boot difference here and the arm sets `second_boot: false`; an emulated twin needs one run.

THE WHOLE READ IS HERE: the `.txt` is the pty log `target/validate/cycle-probe.cap` byte for byte, 57,742 B, espflash's own output included, no range trimmed, so there is no separate `raw/` copy to make. The long binary-looking line is the ROM and the second-stage bootloader at 115200 read by a monitor at 921600, and the in-band header is at the end of it (`grep -a`): `[fw-checks-header] {"schema":1,"payload":"cycle-probe","chip":"esp32v3","firmware_commit":"c976f17a9a1e","firmware_features":"default,esp32,float-f32,server,test_cycle_probe","firmware_dirty":false}`.
